title: Het straattaal-stoplicht
summary: Slang by traffic-light: green words you can use freely, yellow words that need the right room, and why Dutch red-tier cursing is one to leave alone

blocks.title: Three lights
blocks.body: Real Dutch is full of slang, and it comes in three tiers. **Green** = say it to anyone, anywhere. **Yellow** = fine with friends, risky at work or with strangers — read the room. **Red** = leave it alone; we'll explain why. The goal today isn't to swear — it's to know which light you're on, so you sound natural *and* safe.
blocks.callout: When in doubt, treat a word as one light redder than you think.

blocks.title: 🟢 Green — use freely
blocks.body: These are the warm, everyday words that make you sound Dutch and cost you nothing. Sprinkle them liberally.

rows: nice, tasty, 'nicely' — approval for food, weather, a nap, anything
cozy, convivial — the national good-vibe word
cool, great — warm and informal, totally fine
relaxed, easygoing — borrowed from English, everyday
reassuring particle — 'no worries': *het is goed, hoor*

blocks.title: Tap to hear the green tier
🟡 Yellow — read the room
blocks.body: Fine with friends, clangy with your boss or landlord. **vet** (literally 'fat') = 'awesome' — but it reads young. **echt niet** = 'no way'. **balen** / *ik baal ervan* = 'what a bummer / that bugs me' — mild and mostly safe. **kut** is very common as an interjection for frustration (*kut, ik ben mijn pas vergeten*), but it's literally crude — keep it for close friends, never in a job interview.
blocks.callout: Yellow = same word, wrong room, wrong impression.

pairs.right: Vet, man! — great, but reads teenage
pairs.note: Both are positive; *vet* just pins your age and your informality.

pairs.right: cruder frustration words — close friends only
pairs.note: Same disappointment, different register. When unsure, reach for the greener option.

blocks.title: 🔴 Red — know it, don't use it
blocks.body: Dutch has a kind of swearing found almost nowhere else: its harshest curses are built on the **names of serious diseases** (cancer, typhus, cholera). These are the most taboo words the language has — heavier than the English f-word, and genuinely wounding. Used *at* a person, they're a real insult, not banter, and many Dutch people find them shocking. We name this so you understand it when you hear it — that flinch on a Dutch face is real. As a learner: there's zero upside and a lot of downside. Leave the red tier alone.
blocks.callout: If you're ever unsure whether a word is safe, that uncertainty is your answer: don't.

blocks.prompt: Je baas vraagt hoe je weekend was. Welke reactie is overal veilig?
blocks.explain: Green tier fits any listener. *Vet* reads teenage in a work setting, and *kut* is crude — fine with a mate, wrong with a boss.

blocks.prompt: Which word is 'green' — safe with anyone, including strangers and elders?
blocks.explain: *tof* is warm, positive and universally fine. *vet* is yellow (reads young); the third belongs to the crude pile.

blocks.prompt: A friend shows off their new bike and it's great. Give a warm, green-light reaction (two words).
blocks.hint: Green tier only — nothing you'd regret at work.
blocks.explain: *Wat tof!* or *Wat leuk!* — pure green: warm, safe, unmistakably Dutch.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the (very green) reaction.
Noem drie 'groene' woorden die je vanaf nu vaak wilt gebruiken, en leg in het Nederlands uit waarom straattaal per situatie verschilt.
